claim_text: In these verses *nephesh* is the person, the one who answers for sin; it is not a faculty inside the person. The soul is the accountable, answerable self (D §3.1, §11.2)
Souls are saved from death and purified (Jam 5:20; 1Pe 1:22)
Animals almost never have *rûaḥ*; Ecc 3:21 is the only exception; Gen 7:22 uses *neshamah*, not *rûaḥ*

The spirit is prominent in worship and is what is committed to God at death (E §13.4). Pro 20:27 uses *neshamah* "breath", not *rûaḥ* [lexical], and is outside the reading. The human spirit is equally temper, trouble and provocation (Pro 29:11; Gen 41:8; Act 17:16)

The original itself cites "the Lord who made our souls" (Jer 38:16). Also: "The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life" (Job 33:4). Both are made by God. The distinct-origins argument does not hold

Most of these verses speak of the soul delivered or brought up from Sheol: a living person rescued from death. Corrected 2026-10-04 (#1950): of 15 soul-delivered verses, 12 are rescue from dying; Psa 49:15 (set against the death of all, 49:10) and Psa 16:10 (as Act 2:27, 31 read it) look beyond death; Psa 89:48 says no one can. The verdict holds: no verse gives soul and spirit different destinations. Sheol here is death and the grave, not a destination distinct from the spirit's. Ecc 3:21 leaves the spirit's destination open ("Who knows?"). The "different destinations" argument, which the original called "the most compelling evidence", does not hold (G §16.4; dep §3.9)
"The body apart from the spirit is dead" (Jam 2:26)
New heart and new spirit are both needed (Eze 11:19; 36:26)

The shape stands. Distinct Hebrew verses by sense: soul 230, life 180, myself 126, person 83, appetite 45, dead body 13, creature 12, neck 2. Greek: soul 46, life 33, person 8, myself 6. Add throat / neck (stocktake §2)
Most soul-and-death verses are about life delivered from death, not survival after it (see 3-9). The survival texts (Mat 10:28; Rev 6:9) stand

original_chapter: Chapter 8 — The Spirit's fruit (the theological claims only)

claim_text: Most "spirit of …" phrases name a disposition that comes upon a person; the verse does not name a being. The same phrasing is used for good gifts: a spirit of wisdom, skill, grace, justice. Some are given by God: "the Lord has poured out upon you a spirit of deep sleep" (Isa 29:10); the harmful spirit "from the Lord" (1Sa 16:14); God "sent an evil spirit" (Judg 9:23); the Lord "put a lying spirit" in the prophets' mouths (1Ki 22:23). 2Ti 1:7 says "God gave us a spirit not of fear". Spirit-beings are real (unclean spirits cast out; the spirit of divination, Act 16:16), but the one-to-one mapping to vice families is not in the text (SC; dep §2.3c; D §11.4)

The body's redemption at the end stands (Rom 8:23; 1Co 15:42–44), but these are not in the reading and are held. The text renews the inner self "day by day" (2Co 4:16); renewal is both God's gift (Eze 36:26) and the person's task (Eze 18:31). Assigning each phase to one component is not stated
